newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean strike leaders leave church grounds.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean strike leaders leave church grounds.

text.p: South Korea's strike leaders left Seoul's Myongdong Cathedral on Friday after leading almost a month of protests against a controversial labour law from the church grounds, witnesses said.
Witnesses said Kwon Young-kil, leader of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, and a number of deputies walked out of the cathedral grounds and proceeded into nearby shopping alleys.
The confederation leaders set up their strike headquarters in the church on December 26 when the ruling New Korea Party rammed the labour bill through parliament.
They had also sought sanctuary there to avoid arrest after directing wildcat strikes in protest at the law.

But President Kim Young-sam, in a stunning concession during a meeting with opposition leaders on Tuesday, said he would instruct officials to suspend arrest warrants against the unionists. Kim also agreed to reopen debate over the law. Kwon embraced a group of Catholic priests before leaving.
